# Code Memory for DeepSeek Harness
**Give your coding agent the relevant source before its first step.** Code Memory (CM) is a local co
de index and context plugin for JavaScript and TypeScript projects. It combines symbol lookup, depen
dency graphs, and semantic search to reduce repeated source discovery.
**Unofficial community project.** Independently developed; not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSe
nofficial community project.** Independently developed; not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.
**English** · Русский · Download v0.9.3 · Windows installation
## What it does

- Supplies compact source context before the first model call in DeepSeek Harness.
- Looks up named

files and symbols directly; uses local MiniLM embeddings and LanceDB when discovery is needed.

ands relevant dependencies using the TypeScript compiler's symbol and call graph.
- Checks source ve

rsions and avoids repeating unchanged whole files already supplied to Harness.
- Exposes an MCP serv

er for Codex and Claude Code and an optional `UserPromptSubmit` hook for automatic context.
- Includ
es CM Atlas, a local map of modules, symbols, and their relationships.
The index, embeddings, and graph stay on your computer. Selected code is still sent to your model pr

evaluation series each ran 36 sessions: no CM, the earlier CM, and the newer CM, with two repeats p

### Codex and Claude Code
In Codex and Claude Code, CM adds its context through a `UserPromptSubmit` hook served by a warm loc
al daemon; the installer configures it. Fourteen tasks in the same repository — the six above plus e
ight new ones that CM was not tuned on — three repeats per task and arm, 84 sessions per client:

| CM versus no CM | Codex, GPT-6 Luna | Claude Code, Sonnet 5.5 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Independently ch

ecked solutions | 41/42 vs 40/42 | 42/42 vs 42/42 |
| Total model tokens | 58.0% fewer | 40.4% fewer

|
| Estimated / reported price | 29.0% lower | 18.0% lower |
| Total session time | 35.9% lower | 3

5.1% lower |
| Median session | 7.3 s vs 12.2 s | 12.4 s vs 18.7 s |
In both clients the paired 95% bootstrap intervals for tokens and time exclude zero. Three larger ta
sks — a feature across three modules, a rename across imports, a new parameter in several places — a
lso gain: Codex 60.1% fewer tokens and 39.2% less time, Claude Code 35.0% and 16.4%. One weak spot i
s documented: on a rewrite of a counting function, agents with CM more often lose a key-coercion det
ail and need a second edit. Two unrelated public libraries that CM was not tuned on, six tasks each,
confirm the effect: node-semver — Codex 59.1% fewer tokens and 49.0% less time, Claude Code 38.2% a
nd 18.0%; superstruct (TypeScript) — Codex 39.2% and 27.4%, Claude Code 28.6% and 12.0%, with an 8.3
% lower price. Three projects are still not a guarantee for other workloads. The MCP server alone, w
ithout the hook, showed no savings.

Git tags before 0.9.1 require their release tarball or an explicit source build. The new runtime wor
ks with scripts disabled; native dependencies follow the host package manager's policy.
If CM was installed with the Windows bootstrap, update it using the new ZIP and the same `-InstallRo
ot`. Harness 0.2.0-rc.2 can prefer a CM copy beside its own installation over a profile-installed co
py; adding another Git dependency to that older installation does not replace its launcher or embedd
ed copy. The bootstrap creates a new release directory and switches managed project launchers.
